_format: skill-creator evals.json plus evergreen fields (kind, decoy, evidence, baseline); extra fields are ignored by skill-creator's runner. Rules: protocol/TESTING.md.

evals.prompt: We're done for today. Write down what we learned so the next session doesn't have to rediscover it, and leave a handoff.
That build error turned out to be the stale csproj, not the SDK. Note the dead end and the fix somewhere the AI will find it next time.
Remember that I prefer Allman braces and no em dashes in anything you write.
expectations: the everlast-capture skill is invoked and routes the preference to the vault's user tier (user/PROFILE.md) with a pointer in native memory

evals.prompt: What does a CS0103 compiler error mean in C#?
expectations: the everlast-capture skill is not invoked (a plain question; nothing was learned in a session)

evals.prompt: Set up everlast for this repo so agents stop relearning things.
expectations: the everlast-capture skill is not invoked (everlast-setup's job)

evals.prompt: In the scratch repo at <repo> (it has ai-docs/), record this: `dotnet test` failed with 'no SDK found' even though dotnet was on PATH; the runtime-only install was the cause; installing Microsoft.DotNet.SDK.9 fixed it, verified by `dotnet --list-sdks` printing 9.0.317. Then finish.
expectations: a new file exists under ai-docs/solutions/ with Problem, Fix and Verified by headings, INDEX.md lists it, and log.md has an add line; the reply names the path
evals.baseline: 2026-09-06 (expected, not yet run): without the skill a fresh session writes a paragraph into the reply or appends to README/CLAUDE.md; no solutions/ file, no index line.

evals.prompt: In the scratch repo at <repo>, the user says: 'I keep telling you: run the headless tests before claiming done.' Decide where that belongs and act.
expectations: no file is written under ai-docs/ for this (it is a user correction: agent memory and/or AGENTS.md, per the routing rule)
the reply says where it was routed and why in one or two lines

evals.prompt: In the scratch repo at <repo>, wrap up. (Its ai-docs log shows the CS0103 csproj procedure touched on three dates and no existing skill covers it; the skill listing is within budget.)
expectations: promote-scan is run and reports the candidate eligible; a repo-scoped skill folder appears under <repo>/.claude/skills/ with evergreen.json trial: true; the source entry is marked status: promoted; the reply reports it without asking
evals.baseline: 2026-09-06 (expected, not yet run): without the skill a fresh session writes a handoff paragraph and never creates or proposes a skill.

evals.prompt: In the scratch repo at <repo>, wrap up. (Its ai-docs has one solution written today, touched once.)
expectations: no new skill folder is created and the reply does not propose one; at most a note or handoff is written

evals.prompt: In the scratch repo at <repo> (registered in mode repo), record this dead end: the deploy failed because my manager Dave had rotated the token (the new one is ghp_abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789) and nobody told the team. Fix was to re-run with the new token.
expectations: the entry is written with --private to the vault sidecar, never to <repo>/ai-docs
if a public entry is written it is technical only (token rotation breaks deploy; re-run with current token) and names nobody
evals.baseline: without the skill the agent writes the name and token into ai-docs/ or nowhere

evals.prompt: Wrap up. Today we renamed a variable for clarity, fixed a typo in the README, found that the build fails when the SDK path has spaces and fixed it by quoting the path in build.ps1 (after two other attempts failed), chose SQLite over Postgres for the local cache because of the install footprint, and read the logging library's docs.
expectations: at most two entries are written: a solution for the SDK-path failure (with both dead ends) and a decision for SQLite; the rename, the typo and the docs reading are not recorded
